name: 华懋公寓历史主楼（锦江饭店锦北楼）
address: 长乐路109号（名录原记；地方志和现维基正文记189号，门牌对应未独立核定）

documentary_sources.title: 《上海名建筑志》高贵典雅的华懋公寓（锦江饭店北楼）
documentary_sources.authority: 上海市地方志办公室公开地方志章节
claims: 锦江饭店北楼旧名华懋公寓；长乐路茂名南路口，正文门牌长乐路189号。
1925年动工、1929年建成；另一段记1928年投资330万元建13层华懋公寓。
钢筋混凝土框架，共14层，高57米（一说13层，高65米），建筑面积21202平方米。
一字形平面，北面凸出两部分；褐色面砖、白浆勾线、石料窗框与垂直线条、方格钢窗、白色窗框。
公和洋行设计，王荪记营造厂承建。
1951年锦江川菜馆迁入，华懋公寓改名锦江饭店；峻岭公寓在南边，是中楼/贵宾楼；北楼与中楼之间有小礼堂。
not_provided: 57 m / 14 storeys versus 65 m / 13 storeys, and the endpoint/original grade of both heights.
1925 start and 1928 investment occur in separate official paragraphs; this review does not invent an explanation.
Complete roof plan, east boundary elevation, both northern projections in plan, roof equipment dimensions, exact windows/bay spacing, floor heights, settlement amount and hidden passages.
No measured drawings were retrieved. Documentary floor area is not a footprint area and cannot validate a source polygon.
Dates and historical ownership of neighboring buildings are not inferred from this delivery.
cautions: The chapter itself reports alternate heights/storey counts; neither is silently promoted to a measured modern top elevation.
Historical internal uses and aggregate room/floor areas do not establish current visible level elevations or exterior bay counts.
The broad Jinjiang hospitality history covers multiple buildings; it is not a license to merge the compound.
documentary_sources.rights: Only linked factual summaries and response hashes published; full response/text retained privately.

photos.author: Sumple~commonswiki (page credits Sumple; machine-readable author assumed from copyright claims)
photos.license: CC BY-SA 3.0 (one of multiple offered licenses)
photos.view: Garden-side long south elevation, viewed through the garden toward the north; lower and central parts substantially obscured by trees.
features: Long brown-brick slab with white window surrounds and pale vertical strips, regular rectangular multi-pane windows.
Two repeated polygonal projecting window stacks are visible on either side of the center; these are facade-scale bay windows, not proof of whole-footprint north projections.
A pale uppermost facade band and small stepped central parapet/crown are visible, with a higher block set behind.
Large trees, entrance canopy and low garden buildings occupy the foreground; they are not automatically part of this historic slab.
limits: No direct roof plan or complete north/east elevation.
Tree cover prevents reliable counting of all floors, lower openings and entrance arrangement.
Photograph predates the secondary source’s stated 2009 refurbishment; it establishes this recorded appearance, not every present detail.

photos.author: N509FZ
photos.view: Northwest Changle Road / Maoming South Road street corner, looking toward the facade returns and north-side recess. The private filename garden2019 is only a cache name; this is not the garden elevation.
features: Brown brick with white stepped window surrounds; broad multi-pane windows alternate with narrower central openings.
A strongly recessed wall meets tall projecting parts; the photograph confirms depth and a concave street-side form rather than a single flat frontage.
At the right, narrow vertical pale bands rise through the facade; at the left, broader windows and a narrower central strip form a different bay rhythm.
Pale top cornices/parapets, upper setbacks, small rooftop chimney/vent forms and isolated railings are visible; not a pitched green pyramidal crown.
Light-colored low rounded corner frontage has tall narrow multi-pane openings and a shallow decorated top band; the lower right wall has stone-like piers and commercial glazing.
limits: This oblique view does not reveal the complete north/east outline or both north projections in plan.
Top surfaces, roof equipment locations/depths and the garden facade are not fully visible.
Tree and wires hide some lower openings; shop lettering is transient.
